passages.text: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a woman.
She describes herself.
She says, "I am a rose of Sharon."
She also says, "I am a lily of the valleys."

passages.text: Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens.
passages.sermon:
A man speaks about the woman he loves.
He compares her to a lily.
He says she is like a lily among thorns.
He says other women are like thorns.
He says his beloved stands out among other women.
She is beautiful and pure among them.
She is special and different from the rest.
passages.original: כְּשֽׁוֹשַׁנָּה֙ בֵּ֣ין הַחוֹחִ֔ים כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י בֵּ֥ין הַבָּנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Like an apricot tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
passages.sermon:
My beloved is like an apricot tree among the trees of the forest.
He stands out among the young men.
I want to sit in his shade.
I sit there with delight.
His fruit tastes sweet to me.
passages.original: כְּתַפּ֙וּחַ֙ בַּעֲצֵ֣י הַיַּ֔עַר כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י בֵּ֣ין הַבָּנִ֑ים בְּצִלּוֹ֙ חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי וּפִרְי֖וֹ מָת֥וֹק לְחִכִּֽי׃

passages.text: He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.
passages.sermon: My beloved brought me to the house of wine.\r\nHe showed love for me there.\r\nHis love was like a banner over me.
passages.original: הֱבִיאַ֙נִי֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית הַיָּ֔יִן וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה׃

passages.text: Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.
passages.sermon:
The woman speaks to others.
She asks them to help her.
She says, "Sustain me with raisins."
She says, "Refresh me with apples."
She explains why she needs help.
She says, "I am faint with love."
passages.original: סַמְּכ֙וּנִי֙ בָּֽאֲשִׁישׁ֔וֹת רַפְּד֖וּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִ֑ים כִּי־ חוֹלַ֥ת אַהֲבָ֖ה אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
passages.sermon: The beloved is present with me.\r\nHe places his left hand under my head.\r\nHe embraces me with his right arm.

passages.text: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses the daughters of Jerusalem.
The speaker gives them a solemn warning.
The speaker calls on the gazelles and the does of the field as witnesses.
The speaker commands the daughters of Jerusalem.
Do not awaken love.
Do not stir up love.
Wait until love desires to be awakened.
Wait until the right time for love.
passages.original: הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ בִּצְבָא֔וֹת א֖וֹ בְּאַיְל֣וֹת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה אִם־ תָּעִ֧ירוּ׀ וְֽאִם־ תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ אֶת־ הָאַהֲבָ֖ה עַ֥ד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּֽץ׃ס

passages.text: Listen! My beloved approaches. Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a woman who loves her beloved.
\r\nShe hears her beloved’s voice.
\r\nShe says, “Listen!”
\r\nHer beloved is coming.
\r\nShe says, “Look!”
\r\nHer beloved leaps over the mountains.
\r\nHe bounds over the hills.
passages.original: ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֔י הִנֵּה־ זֶ֖ה בָּ֑א מְדַלֵּג֙ עַל־ הֶ֣הָרִ֔ים מְקַפֵּ֖ץ עַל־ הַגְּבָעֽוֹת׃

passages.text: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.
passages.sermon:
My beloved is strong and swift.
He is like a gazelle.
He is like a young stag.
He stands behind our wall.
He looks through the windows.
He peers through the lattice.
passages.original: דּוֹמֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ לִצְבִ֔י א֖וֹ לְעֹ֣פֶר הָֽאַיָּלִ֑ים הִנֵּה־ זֶ֤ה עוֹמֵד֙ אַחַ֣ר כָּתְלֵ֔נוּ מַשְׁגִּ֙יחַ֙ מִן־ הַֽחֲלֹּנ֔וֹת מֵצִ֖יץ מִן־ הַֽחֲרַכִּֽים׃

passages.text: My beloved calls to me, “Arise, my darling. Come away with me, my beautiful one.
passages.sermon:
My beloved speaks to me.
He calls out to me.
He says, "Arise, my darling."
He says, "Come away with me, my beautiful one."
passages.original: עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י ק֥וּמִי לָ֛ךְ רַעְיָתִ֥י יָפָתִ֖י וּלְכִי־ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.
passages.sermon:
Winter is finished.
The cold season has ended.
The rain has stopped.
The rain has gone away.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִנֵּ֥ה הַסְּתָו עָבָ֑ר הַגֶּ֕שֶׁם חָלַ֖ף הָלַ֥ךְ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.
passages.sermon: Flowers now appear in the land.\r\nThe time for singing has arrived.\r\nWe hear the voice of the turtledove in our land.
passages.original: הַנִּצָּנִים֙ נִרְא֣וּ בָאָ֔רֶץ עֵ֥ת הַזָּמִ֖יר הִגִּ֑יעַ וְק֥וֹל הַתּ֖וֹר נִשְׁמַ֥ע בְּאַרְצֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: The fig tree ripens its figs; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come away, my darling; come away with me, my beautiful one.”
passages.sermon:
The fig tree ripens its figs.
The blossoming vines spread their fragrance.
My beloved speaks to his beloved.
He says, "Arise, come away with me, my darling.
Come away with me, my beautiful one."
passages.original: הַתְּאֵנָה֙ חָֽנְטָ֣ה פַגֶּ֔יהָ וְהַגְּפָנִ֥ים׀ סְמָדַ֖ר נָ֣תְנוּ רֵ֑יחַ ק֥וּמִי לְכִי רַעְיָתִ֥י יָפָתִ֖י וּלְכִי־ לָֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his beloved.
He calls her "my dove."
She is in the clefts of the rock.
She is in the secret places of the cliff.
He asks her to show her face.
He asks her to let him hear her voice.
Her voice is sweet.
Her face is lovely.
passages.original: יוֹנָתִ֞י בְּחַגְוֵ֣י הַסֶּ֗לַע בְּסֵ֙תֶר֙ הַמַּדְרֵגָ֔ה הַרְאִ֙ינִי֙ אֶתּ־ מַרְאַ֔יִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִ֖ינִי אֶת־ קוֹלֵ֑ךְ כִּי־ קוֹלֵ֥ךְ עָרֵ֖ב וּמַרְאֵ֥יךְ נָאוֶֽה׃ס

passages.text: Catch for us the foxes— the little foxes that ruin the vineyards— for our vineyards are in bloom.
passages.sermon:
The vineyards are in bloom.
Little foxes ruin the vineyards.
Catch the foxes for us.
Catch the little foxes that cause harm.
passages.original: אֶֽחֱזוּ־ לָ֙נוּ֙ שֽׁוּעָלִ֔ים שֽׁוּעָלִ֥ים קְטַנִּ֖ים מְחַבְּלִ֣ים כְּרָמִ֑ים וּכְרָמֵ֖ינוּ סְמָדַֽר׃

passages.text: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
passages.sermon:
The woman speaks about her beloved.
She says, "My beloved belongs to me."
She also says, "I belong to my beloved."
Her beloved is a shepherd.
He pastures his flock among the lilies.
passages.original: דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃

passages.text: Before the day breaks and shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a woman who loves her beloved.
She speaks to her beloved.
She says, “Before the day breaks, and before the shadows disappear, turn and come back.”
She calls her beloved “my beloved.”
She asks him to be like a gazelle.
She also asks him to be like a young stag.
She wants him to come on the mountains of Bether.
passages.original: עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֙וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים סֹב֩ דְּמֵה־ לְךָ֨ דוֹדִ֜י לִצְבִ֗י א֛וֹ לְעֹ֥פֶר הָאַיָּלִ֖ים עַל־ הָ֥רֵי בָֽתֶר׃ס
